howDoI.q: How do I make the hero fall toward a wall on the left?
How do I make a ceiling the hero can walk on?
How do I make the arrows walk the hero along a wall?
How do I draw a hero on his side or upside down?
How do I make a jump that pushes away from a wall?
How do I make a trench the hero can safely fall into?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Around the Room is a Starter: a small game that shows one Game-Maker idea, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has four short levels, one along each side of a room: the floor, the left wall, the ceiling and the right wall. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The arrows always mean the way they point on the screen: on the left wall, Up walks Yana up the wall, on the ceiling Right walks her right, and on the right wall Down walks her down. The opposite arrow walks her back. Space jumps off the wall. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: The Floor
pages.html:
Level 1: The Floor

The ordinary way comes first, so the other three have something to be compared with. THE FLOOR. GRAVITY PULLS DOWN stands at the start. A BLOCK. JUMP OVER IT stands before a brick block one high, then one two high: walk into the first one and it stops you, so jump. A TRENCH. JUMP ACROSS stands before a gap three blocks wide in the ground. THE ROOM TURNS NEXT stands at the door.

There are five coins, over the blocks and the trench. Notice that the hero walks left, toward the wall the next level is on.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The pull. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor. Every block of air (sky, the coin, the bush, the signs) has Gravity set to Down. The ground blocks (grass, dirt) have no pull and are solid, so Yana stands on them. Game-Maker reads the pull from the block Yana is mostly standing in.
  • The hero. one.chr is a character file with the sequences for each arrow. Left moves her four pixels a frame to the left, Right back to the right, and Up and Down do nothing here. Her pictures are in one.cbl: one block, not two, so she is as tall as the blocks.
  • The jump. The Space sequence has Momentum checked and a first frame that moves her 12 pixels up. That is a push, and the block's pull then takes it back.
  • The trench. In one.map three cells of the ground, grass over dirt, are sky. Falling in is safe: the pull is the same inside.

pages.head: Level 2: The Left Wall
pages.html:
Level 2: The Left Wall

The same course, along the left wall. Gravity pulls left, so the wall is the floor and the hero is on her side with her head to the right. THE LEFT WALL. GRAVITY PULLS LEFT. UP WALKS UP THE WALL stands at the bottom. SPACE JUMPS OFF THE WALL, AND YOU FALL BACK stands above it. Then there is a block two high, two blocks side by side, a trench three blocks wide, and a trench two wide.

Everything you did with Left you do with Up. A sign at the top points to the door. There are five coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The pull. In two.bbl every block of air has Gravity set to Left. The only difference from one.bbl is that setting on each block.
  • The pictures. The ground, the hedge, the door and the scenery in two.bbl are the floor's pictures turned a quarter so the grass faces Yana. The signs, the coins and the sky are not turned: a sign still reads upright, which is part of why this level is a little dizzying.
  • The hero. two.cbl holds Yana turned the same way and two.chr uses her. Up moves her four pixels a frame up the screen (a negative y), Down moves her back, and Left and Right do nothing. She is not climbing: the pull holds her to the wall, as it held her to the floor.
  • The jump. The Space sequence still has Momentum checked, but its first frame now moves her 12 pixels in x, away from the wall, and the block's pull brings her back.
  • The map. two.map is 14 blocks wide and 46 high. The wall carries on past the left edge so nothing shows beyond it.

pages.head: Level 3: The Ceiling
pages.html:
Level 3: The Ceiling

Upside down. Gravity pulls up, so the ceiling is the floor and Yana's head points at the floor. THE CEILING. GRAVITY PULLS UP. RIGHT WALKS RIGHT stands at the start, and SPACE JUMPS DOWN FROM THE CEILING next to it. There are two trenches, one two blocks wide and one three, with A WIDE TRENCH. FALLING UP IS STILL FALLING between them, and blocks that hang from the ceiling.

Most people find this the hardest to read: the blocks hang down and the jumps go down. There are five coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The pull. In three.bbl every block of air has Gravity set to Up. Game-Maker keeps four settings for this, one each for up, down, left and right, and a block can have more than one.
  • The hero. Yana's pictures in three.cbl are turned half a turn, and in three.chr Right walks her to the right (four pixels in x) and Left walks her back. A walk toward the way her face points is the same animation as on the floor.
  • The jump. The Space sequence's first frame moves her 12 pixels down the screen, away from the ceiling.
  • The trench. The cells of the ceiling that are missing show sky above them. A hero who falls into one falls up, and the pull holds her in it until she jumps out.
  • The palette. Each level loads its own palette: only the sky colors change from level to level, noon, sunset, dusk and night.

pages.head: Level 4: The Right Wall
pages.html:
Level 4: The Right Wall

The last side. Gravity pulls right, Yana walks down the wall with her head to the left, and Down is the arrow that walks her on. THE RIGHT WALL. GRAVITY PULLS RIGHT. DOWN WALKS DOWN is at the top. BLOCKS AND TRENCHES. SAME JUMPS, ONE MORE TURN is before a block one high, two blocks two high side by side, a trench three blocks wide and one two wide. THAT WAS ONE LAP. THE LAST DOOR is at the bottom.

If the floor of this lap felt natural by now, remember it did not at the start of level 2. There are five coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 4 is made

  • The pull. four.bbl has Gravity set to Right on every block of air.
  • The hero. four.chr mirrors level 2: Down walks her four pixels a frame down the screen, Up back up, and Space pushes her 12 pixels to the left, away from the wall. Her pictures in four.cbl are turned the other way.
  • A lap. The four levels are one course laid along a floor, a left wall, a ceiling and a right wall, one quarter turn each. A lap goes clockwise: left along the floor, up the left wall, right along the ceiling, down the right wall.
  • Why four character files. A level's scene names its own character file and character blocks, so each level can have the hero drawn its own way and with its own keys. Inside a level the hero's keys and pictures do not change.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot turn the room. There is no setting that rotates the screen or a map. A wall level has its own pictures, drawn turned, and a block set where each pull points the same way.
  • It cannot turn the hero. Each pose in each direction is a picture you draw. Yana has four sets of pictures here, one a level.
  • The hero's keys do not change inside a level. A level that pulled the hero a different way halfway would keep the same keys and pictures. That is why each wall is its own level and the turn between them is a door.
  • The pull is read from one block. It is the block the hero is mostly standing in, so half over a trench the middle decides.
  • A jump is a push, not a height. The push is 12 pixels and the pull takes it back one step a frame, the same size everywhere: a block can pull a way or not, but not harder. A falling hero never goes faster than 11 pixels a frame.
  • The arrows toward and away from the wall have nothing to do unless you give them a sequence.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Set Gravity on one sky block of level 2 to Down and watch Yana fall through the middle of the wall.
  • Give a block two settings, Left and Down, and watch the pull slide her along.
  • Change the push in a hero's Space sequence from 12 to 8.
  • Make a fifth level on the wall of your own: copy level 2, and take the signs out.
  • Draw a different hero in two.cbl.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer walks once around a room: along the floor, up the left wall, along the ceiling upside down and down the right wall. Each turn of the room is another level, with the same blocks to jump and trenches to cross, and your hands have to keep up. The trick is a setting on each block: which way it pulls. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a block's Gravity.
features: Four levels: the floor, the left wall, the ceiling and the right wall
The hero is drawn turned to face each wall
Gravity is a setting of each block
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Four short levels that go once around a room: the floor, up the left wall, along the ceiling upside down, and down the right wall. The hero is drawn turned on each one and jumps the same blocks and trenches every time. Nothing in Game-Maker turns a room. Each block has a setting for which way it pulls, and the arrows are the hero's own keys. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change one block's Gravity.

57.long: Jump off the wall, away from the surface you stand on. Steer along the wall with the arrow while you are in the air.

72.long: Walk up. Up the left wall it walks forward; down the right wall it walks back.

75.long: Walk left. On the floor it walks forward; on the ceiling it walks back.

77.long: Walk right. On the ceiling it walks forward; on the floor it walks back.

80.long: Walk down. Down the right wall it walks forward; up the left wall it walks back.
